channel.title: AgentSlang blog
channel.description: Notes from building a language for models.

item.title: Four Imports and a Short List: How ASL Fences In Agent-Written Code
item.description: How ASL fences in agent-written code with explicit effect signatures, a small declared host adapter, and a wasm32 target that runs on four host imports and refuses everything else at compile time.

item.title: Many Calls in One Frame: ASN Wire Batches vs. Chatty JSON-RPC
item.description: How ASN S-expression frames carry batched tool calls and structured (:batch ...) receipts in one round trip without double-escaping code inside JSON-RPC envelopes.

item.title: Edit by Symbol, Not by Line Number: How the ASL Toolbelt Keeps Batch Patches Exact
item.description: How the asl toolbelt addresses code by symbol name and exact text across multi-step batches, returning structured receipts instead of silently patching shifted line numbers.

item.title: Constrained Decoding for Small Local Models: How ASL Keeps 3B Agents on the Rails
item.description: How ASL's regular S-expression grammar and the asl-slm token-masking state machine keep small local models on Apple Silicon generating balanced, valid forms.

item.title: Keeping 3B Local Models Parse-Clean: Why Explicit S-Expressions Beat Significant Whitespace
item.description: Why explicit prefix S-expressions and pre-run balance checks let small local models edit nested logic without tripping over Python indentation cascades.

item.title: One Form per Call, One Batch per Turn: Why ASL Frames Agent Messages as S-Expressions
item.description: How ASL frames code, data and batched tool calls in one S-expression notation so agent messages travel without JSON-RPC string-escaping overhead.

item.title: Tests at the Speed of Thought: ASL's Container-Free Test Loop and the WebAssembly Sandbox Ahead
item.description: How asl test runs fast container-free verification today, and how ASL's LLVM wasm32 backend sets up in-memory WebAssembly sandboxes for agent repair loops.

item.title: Designed for Left-to-Right Generation: Why ASL Replaces Indentation and Borrow Puzzles with Prefix Forms
item.description: Why left-to-right transformer generation clashes with Python indentation and Rust borrow constraints, and how ASL's prefix S-expressions and pre-run checker remove the syntax repair loop.

item.title: Every Test Answers with a Receipt: Assertion Counts and Telemetry in ASL
item.description: How asl test turns verification into structured evidence—refusing vacuous suites, reporting executed assertion counts in every receipt, and exposing runtime memory telemetry.

item.title: Memory That Follows the Tree: Git-Tracked ASN Ledgers and Tiered Aggregation in ASL
item.description: How ASL stores agent memory as git-tracked ASN S-expression ledgers queried on demand rather than flat context dumps, and the tree-aggregated tiers built on top.

item.title: Batch Tool Calls and Staged Transactions: Why Agents Need More Than a Bash Wrapper
item.description: How the asl toolbelt replaces fragile bash subprocesses with batched symbol reads, session-isolated staged edits, pre-run checker gates and atomic (:txn ...) rollbacks.

item.title: Whole Words, Fewer Tokens: Why ASL Uses camelCase Names Built for BPE Tokenizers
item.description: Why whole-word camelCase identifiers tokenize more cleanly under BPE than vowelless abbreviations, keep symbol queries exact, and let agents predict builtin names.

item.title: The Model Proposes, the Toolchain Verifies: ASL's Split Between Agent ALU and Deterministic Host
item.description: How ASL pairs the language model with a deterministic toolchain for symbol lookup, staged transactions and static verification over one batched ASN contract.

item.title: One Grammar for Code, Data, Markup and Queries: Closing the Agent Operational Circle
item.description: How one checked S-expression notation across code, data ledgers, batched tool calls, HTML/SVG views and SQL queries removes multi-format escaping traps.

item.title: Fewer Moving Parts: How ASL Keeps Agent-Built Infrastructure Small
item.description: How one language for code, data and batched tool calls replaces sprawling orchestration frameworks with small, gate-verified steps and readable receipts.

item.title: Vector Graphics as Checked S-Expressions: How ASL Builds SVG and HTML Without XML Boilerplate
item.description: How agents author SVG diagrams and HTML5 interfaces as checked S-expression forms in ASL, avoiding XML closing-tag blowup and mid-element truncation.

item.title: Memory That Moves With the Code: Git-Versioned Agent Ledgers and In-Process Recall
item.description: How ASL stores agent findings and plans in git-tracked ASN ledgers that branch, diff and merge alongside the code, paired with in-process vector recall.

item.title: One Query Value, Four Dialects: How ASL Renders SQL for Postgres, SQLite, MySQL & ClickHouse
item.description: How asl-sql represents relational queries as typed ASL values and renders them with bound parameters for PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL and ClickHouse.

item.title: From This WebAssembly Page to an In-Browser Agent Sandbox: Running ASL with Zero Backend Servers
item.description: How ASL compiles through LLVM to self-contained wasm32 modules on four host imports—powering this site today and laying the foundation for in-browser agent sandboxes.

item.title: Let the Checker Hold the Line: Closure Checks, Honest Tests and Anti-Hallucination Firewalls
item.description: How ASL replaces prompt-level warnings with machine-enforced boundaries: static name and arity checks, non-vacuous test gates, workspace path jails and verifiable receipts.

item.title: One Glue Language, Native and WebAssembly: Ending Multi-Language Drift in ASL
item.description: How compiling one checked ASL source through LLVM to native binaries and wasm32 modules eliminates semantic drift between backend tools and browser runtimes.

item.title: Topology, Cost and Boundaries: How ASL Observes Agent Swarms Through Receipts
item.description: How ASL replaces raw log dumps with structured queries and ASN receipts over module topology, token cost and capability boundaries.

item.title: A Toolbelt Built for Agents: Symbol Reads, Staged Edits and One Batch of Receipts
item.description: How the asl toolbelt batches symbol queries, bounded reads, staged edits and static checks into a single call answered by structured ASN receipts.

item.title: Typed Frames, Not Chatter: The Design of ASL's Inter-Agent Protocol (AgP)
item.description: How AgP replaces verbose natural-language handoffs between agents with sigil-headed S-expression frames, a closed error taxonomy and context-isolated receipts.

item.title: Structural Compaction Over Abbreviation: How ASN Tables and Batches Keep Agent Payloads Lean
item.description: Measured under BPE tokenizers: why abbreviating keywords saves nothing, while ASN tabular schemas and positional frames cut repeated-key overhead by 40% to 64.7% against spaced JSON.

item.title: Written for the Model, Checked for the Human: Why ASL Uses S-Expressions and Closed Variants
item.description: How single-pass S-expressions, closed algebraic variants and explicit effect markers give models an unambiguous grammar and give humans a checker verdict they can trust.

item.title: Read the Interface, Not the File: How ASL Outline and Symbol Queries Keep Agent Context Sharp
item.description: How (:intel :op outline), (:read :symbol) and explicit module export lists let agents inspect only the public interface they need instead of dumping whole files into context.
